7Rename three cards2026-11-25The 3-cards shown in the container at the top represent the 3 processes required for MedID: a photo, descriptive notes, and lookup / identify. 8Switch above cards2026-11-25The format / layout needs a few changes. I like the switch-style sliding button to select between Container and Medication. That is well done! But let's position that sliding choice between the two at the top--just after the introductory paragraph following MedID, just before the 3 colored cards. Critically, update our build scripts to remember and often choose the switch-style selection, a design style we will use more widely as we build material. Always attempt to present that switch option to me in cases where we are deciding between 2 options, or multiple outcomes, as part of our build script for all guides. The switch may include larger number of options--3, 4, etc. In those cases, the selected button shifts to whichever choice was made, as it does currently between these two options.
9Container becomes Packaging2026-11-25Let's use better phrases: instead of Container, lets use the word Packaging. Sometimes meds are in plastic bags, bottles, paper packs, etc. Packaging could be any of those. The word "container" is a little too specific. Our MedID app can use any type of packaging to dig for information about the medication.
10Medication tab meaning2026-11-25The Medication tab, by contrast, is more obvious--it's a pill, vial of something, powder, etc. While still a potentially very large category, the app will discern that the medication is outside of, or removed from, any packaging that once held the medication.
11Selected bubble green2026-11-25Add an action for the sliding choice button that activates any time one of the two options is selected (Container or Medication): when clicked the background color of the selected and displayed bubble text changes color to the same soft green color shown as the background of the Identify card. Visually, that color and font switch to bold signifies the selection was made, and the associated script path will then run specific to that activated selection.
12Consolidate three cards2026-11-25Consolidate and better organize the two disparate sections in the middle of the guide that represent nearly the same task flow. We only need 3 cards, as renamed above: Photo Upload, Add Notes, and Identify Med to represent the 3 required steps for medication identification. Reducing to 3 cards total simplifies the MedID workflow, improves efficiency and speed, and makes better use of the screen space which must be optimized for mobile, desktop and light/dark themes.
13Wire card actions2026-11-25Configure each card to perform the associated action represented in the lower part of the guide and stated explicitly here: Photo Upload (the first card) will show 2 icons below the title. Both must be created using our Peptopia build standard for icons / push buttons. For examples to reference while building, remember that we do NOT create these from scratch. Specifically, look at the Printer icon--it shows a neon line drawing and is see-through / holographic. Both new icons must be created in that style, though you are free to select the neon color to use. Just remember the images you use are not flat, solid shapes. They are transparent neon glowing line drawings like the Home and printer button show currently. The moment the user begins on the Photo Upload card--indicated by the mouse over card action--you will "light up" the Photo Upload card by changing the border color to a bright neon green--light a green light used in traffic. That border color shall remain that color (activated) until the user finishes with photo actions. Both new icons will be placed on the same line, centered on their horizontal center, after exactly one line of empty space below the new card title - Photo. The first icon on the left will be based on the camera you currently show on "Snap a pic - upload photo." Configure the icon as we did the nav icons in the header--the glass push button, etc. These styles are well documented, so configure them accordingly. We have built at least 20 icons in the same style; your instructions should be perfectly clear by this point to not create from scratch, but to copy and modify an existing "correct" icon for your baseline. Once chosen, then style the camera shape as a neon outlined see through /holographic translucent icon enlarged to almost the same size as it's circular container. The circle border and the neon line outline of the camera shall be the same color. And, like all icons, you add the glassy sparkle top left corner and the gentle halo shadowing. Again, do not make me resort to feeding all these instructions again. As one way you could accomplish this, copy the Peptopia logo; remove the running girl, and replace with the neon line drawing of the camera. However the neon color you choose for the shape and the border must be unique for each new icon, and it will not be the magenta shown on the Peptopia logo. It's best to show the camera on an angle, if possible, not head on exactly like the camera currently showing. Link that first option to the camera app, if possible. If not provide simple short instructions to the user through a popup that states something like "Use your camera app to photo the med, with packaging if possible". Once the user takes the photo, you will hold that in cache and collect any notes collected on the next step, waiting for the user to click the button for the third and final step--Identify Med. The second icon on the Photo Upload card will show a graphic you choose and create from a unique neon color not currently represented by other nav icons. Naturally, it represents the upload function. Users click this upload button if they already have a photo of the med. That part is simple, and is how the current "Snap a pic--upload photo" button works. As soon as the pic is attached and you have it in cache, the popups close and MedId changes the border color of the Add Notes card to "light up" the card (show it as activated) by changing the border color to a bright neon green--an intense neon green light similar to those used in traffic signaling.
14Notes popup field2026-11-25With the photo in cache, you will then allow the user to add notes. Add a popup data entry field configured the way the current Notes field is now--a container that is the same width as the content for the page. That width will vary of course between desktop, a wider field, and mobile, narrow. But in both cases, allow the field to auto expand from one line to more as the user adds information. The may add multiple sentences, and the field needs to accept up to 50 words total. Do not require that notes be added; notes are optional. The user can click out of the popup by clicking Submit through a button shown underneath the notes input field, or the user can escape the popup from a red x (our default exit icon from the icon store) positioned in upper right corner and sized the same size as the nav icons top of page. Alternatively, the user can just click anywhere outside the popup container to return to the MedID screen. Again, notes are not required, but the field must be auto-formatted based on the users screen and how many words (if any) they type.
15Spinner results container2026-11-25With the photo and notes in hand, you will "light up" the Identify Med card by changing the border color to a bright neon green--light a green light used in traffic. At that point, conduct your research quickly and efficiently, showing a spinning circular image in the center of the page that is double the size of the standard icon size for the page. Show an alert while that icon spins--something like "Researching, wait one minute, please." As soon as the results are known, open a new results container located no further than one empty line of text below the row of action cards. Size the results window by indenting 5 spaces from left and 5 spaces from right on desktop screens, and only couple character spaces on mobile screens.
16Essential Drugs format2026-11-25Medication identification should always list exactly how they are presented on this page: https://x-peps.com/admin-portal/essential-drugs.html Always list the drug name (both chemical and common, if available, each separated by a | symbol), the class, the indication (USED FOR) and then the warnings (WATCH FOR). Format the results that display exactly the way the chart on the reference link looks. Use the exact same table format, led with a title to indicate which body system is affected, and even the yellow highlighted column. These conventions of formatting are extremely important in medication identification. We must know both the manufacturer (chemical) drug name and the more common name, the class, the indication, and any warnings. If any of that information is unavailable in the result, simply leave that cell blank. The results presented in the results container opened by Identify Med must be formatted exactly like the chart on the reference link, including colors, fonts, and other details.
